s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
Laboratory studies are within normal limits

differentials: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology of lesions

shortlist.label: Urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Intensely pruritic skin lesions with well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and central clearing of lesions

shortlist.label: Annular erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetrically distributed lesions on the anterior thighs in a mirror-image pattern

raw.rationale: The patient's lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing, which is characteristic of Erythema annulare centrifugum. The lesions also occur in recurrent outbreaks and resolve spontaneously without residual injury, consistent with this condition.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Typically associated with systemic symptoms and target lesions, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: Lesions are not described as wheals and do not have the typical raised, itchy appearance of hives

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Laboratory studies are within normal limits, and there is no evidence of vasculitis on examination

rejected.label: Annular erythema
rejected.why: While the lesions have an annular appearance, the description is more consistent with Erythema annulare centrifugum, which is a more specific diagnosis
